raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through. I'm going to plan the whole year — wheat first since it's the main thing on this land, then corn after.

---

This year I'll do the same as my father did and what I've been doing 15 years now — wheat in October, corn after the wheat in June. No reason to change. Land works fine that way, neighbors all do the same.

**Wheat** — I'll go in around October 8th or 10th, that's when the village plants. I'll buy the same seed from the agro-shop in town that I used last year, the kind my brother-in-law uses too — gets fair ears. Before plowing I'll spread two bags of the compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 — that's about 80 jin per mu. Father always said you can't skimp on the base or the wheat won't tiller right. Then plow it in with the rotary tiller, hire that done.

I winter-water once in November before the ground freezes — helps it through the cold months. In spring when the wheat stands up at jointing, I spread one bag of urea per mu, about 40 jin, and water it in then. Water again at heading time if it hasn't rained — that water is the most important one for the grain to fill. So three waterings if the sky doesn't help me. Each watering costs about 30 yuan a mu in pumping fees, so I don't do extra.

I spray once in early spring for the weeds, a cheap herbicide my neighbor told me about. Don't bother with bug spray unless I see something.

Wheat comes off early-to-mid June. I hire the combine — can't cut 10 mu by hand, costs about 50 yuan a mu but it's done in an hour. Then it's a race to get the corn in.

**Corn** — within a week of cutting the wheat I borrow my cousin's no-till seeder and plant straight into the stubble. No plowing — no time. Same hybrid as last year, the shop man said it does well here, did okay for me. Through the seeder I put down about 40 jin per mu of compound, that's the base. When the corn is about knee-high in July I spread one bag of urea per mu between the rows.

Corn — usually we get enough rain in July and August so I don't always water. If it stays dry I'll water once at the time when the silk comes out, that's the important time. Spray once for weeds when the corn is small. Watch for borers — if I see them eating into the stalks I'll spray once, otherwise no.

Corn comes off end of September, just in time to clear the field for the wheat again.

My wife and I do most of the work. My oldest boy is in middle school, helps on weekends and during the busy times. The two younger kids and my mother stay out of the field. My brother does construction work in town some months, sends money home. With 6 mouths and only 10 mu I can't be putting on extra fertilizer I don't need or watering more than necessary — every yuan has to count for something.

Normal year I get 800 jin of wheat per mu and 900 jin of corn per mu. Good year a bit more, bad year less. That's how it goes.
